title: Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states
main_claim: Take a nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian on an open L x L square lattice with bounded terms, a unique ground state Omega and a gap Delta for the full Hamiltonian only. Then there is a PEPS on the same grid with bond dimension C L^c that approximates Omega to normalized vector error at most L^{-1}. The constants depend only on q, J and Delta.
coverage:
I read every section in build/sections (00 to 08). I checked these parts line by line:
(a) Thm 4.2, density compression. Lemma 4.1 (effect elimination by cyclic averaging, error m^{-1/2}). The Gaussian fourth-moment covariance identity. The fact that the affected-side map O is a contraction on all free inputs. The 4-2-4 Schatten Holder step and the weighted Hilbert-Schmidt bound, which together give E||Z||_1 <= k^{-s/2} with no dependence on dimension. The subset-expansion cost Q^s. The locality of the doubled network, with each U_j acting locally per party.
(b) Prop 3.1, adaptive patch constraint. Stationarity giving [L_j, rho_j] = 0 in descending order. The KKT/clipped eigenvalue formula. The cosh(ay)-1 <= a^2(cosh y - 1) bound and the row/column Cauchy-Schwarz, which give energy <= 36 q^2 J kappa^2. The gap leading to marginal trace distance 1/16. The Markov tail rank. Tr T_j <= 1/4. The Dini-derivative growth bound. The first-head expansion and the choice of R_0. The orthogonalization at variable radii.
(c) Lemma 2.3, information reset. The swap/purity overlap z >= e^{-2b}. The two-sided Gaussian filter. The Lieb-Robinson localization and Duhamel step. The polar-unitary bound. That the support avoids both cores. The Winter continuity exponent arithmetic: L^{2 - r*/2} = L^{-p-3}.
(d) Lemma 2.2, cell CMI. The purity identity I(U:C|Z) = I(U:C|W) for family-1 tiles and the generation count. Prop 2.4 (angular): the induction margins (1.5a'+d < 2a', clearance (a/2-3a'-d)s) and the choice of D.
(e) Lemmas 5.x. The group tensor nuclear-norm bound, the open-leg two-owner argument in the small-patch rewrite, the birth/death splitting, and the exchange intertwining (D_U F_A F_Y = D_U F_T).
(f) Section 6. I re-derived the band-word sequence (aux word, main word after the lens exchange, the deaths and births). I checked the margins in Lemma 6.2 and the lifetime invariant.
(g) Section 7. The column-extraction lemma, the dyadic-anchor routing congestion including the 2-adic row argument, folding (factor 4), and the error budget (L^{-17}, L^{-57}, L^{-5}).
I verified only structurally: the compactness and finite-pattern constants in Section 6 (point treatment, footprint two-owner test), and the internals of the companion area-law and amplification results. I spot-checked that the companion's template definition allows the cut A = Lambda, i.e. Z empty.
sibling_notes: The family-265 board had one entry: the companion 'A two-dimensional area law from a global spectral gap' (rank 115), reported no_gap_found. It matters because this paper imports its area law, sublinear collar, positive replacement and amplification as black boxes, used in Prop 2.1 and Prop 3.1. The sibling found nothing wrong in those inputs, and I found no misuse of their hypotheses here. Only the full-system gap is assumed, there is no subsystem gap, and the A = Lambda case of the template is allowed.
